pr_title: Improve schedule note of .after/.before & encourage to use .chain ins…
pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #14552 
- Make the current note of `before` and `after` understandable. 
    - > The given set is not implicitly added to the schedule when this system set is added.

## Solution

- Replace note in docs of [`after` and `before`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/trait.IntoSystemConfigs.html#method.before) 
- Note of after was removed completely, and links to `before`, because they notes would be identical.
- Also encourage to use `.chain`, which is much simpler and safer to use

## Testing

- Checked the docs after running `cargo doc` and `cargo run -p ci -- lints`
- Are there any parts that need more testing?
  - no need to test, but please review the text. If it is still including the intended message and especially if its understandable.
pr_comments:
@janhohenheim 

Thanks for pointing it out.

> I think this version is somewhat misleading. 

I think the the example in https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/trait.IntoSystemConfigs.html#method.before might be misleading as well. `animate_targets` doesn't seem to me in the same `Set`. For a beginner this quite confusing. It is in [line 7 of the example](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/src/animated_fox/animated_fox.rs.html#7) and therefore in `use bevy::{ animation::{ animate_targets, ...`  - why would that work or is that an error in the example? Or indeed there is a mistake in the suggested Note.

I think we could improve not only the Notes, but examples and the description. Maybe emphasize, when dependencies are created, so it does not have to be in the Notes. 

I also think the sentence `It's safe and won't cause any problems or errors` is obsolete.

Looking great now, thanks! I just fixed a bug in the wild caused by this (https://github.com/kaosat-dev/Blenvy/pull/243), so let's hope this documentation helps prevent them in the future :)
Looks like you need a quick `cargo fmt` and it's good to go.

>     /// If you configure two [`SystemSet`]s like `(GameSystem::A).after(GameSystem::B)` or `(GameSystem::A).before(GameSystem::B)`, the `GameSystem::B` will not be automatically scheduled.

This line doesn't make any sense to me: system sets can't be scheduled, only applied to systems which are scheduled.

Fair enough, I see what you mean. The current docs (before this PR) call this "adding the set to the schedule", but the correct phrase would be something like "adding the systems inside the set to the schedule"

so the changes in the review won't be enough? So System set can't be scheduled, but still using system inside the set would more likely happen as an error.

What I wonder is why is that possible at all. Does a check, wouldn't help. If it can't be scheduled, it should error. But that would be a different issue.

So what else need's to be corrected?
So far we have the suggestion from @alice-i-cecile  and then comments about systems and system set from @janhohenheim and instead of `two ['SystemSet']s` it's `two ['System']s`

I'd like to get a confirmation by @alice-i-cecile on whether to really change the docs to mention systems instead of system sets. I've laid down my argument as to why I think writing about system sets is more beneficial to a reader, but ultimately I trust her judgment either way :)

> So far we have the suggestion from @alice-i-cecile and then comments about systems and system set from @janhohenheim and instead of two ['SystemSet']s it's two ['System']s

This is the change that I think is most important. I would also remove the line about `configure_sets` completely. Everything else is just style / wording suggestions.

The fundamental model here is that when we call `add_systems(Update, my_system.before(other_system))`, `my_system` is being used as a system, while `other_system` represents the system set that `other_system` is added to. There's no way to add a system set to a schedule as it's basically a "tag" / metadata, and has no behavior.

By contrast, calling `.add_systems(Update, (my_system, other_system)).chain()` is a modifier on `.add_systems(Update, (my_system, other_system))`, which adds the two systems to the system schedule, and then creates ordering links between them.

> By contrast, calling .add_systems(Update, (my_system, other_system)).chain() is a modifier on .add_systems(Update, (my_system, other_system)), which adds the two systems to the system schedule, and then creates ordering links between them.

So `.add_systems(Update, (my_system, other_system))` would add to the schedule, but not create ordering link. I don't know if that could be a usful information for the [method.add_systems](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_systems)
Thanks for your patience; I really appreciate you both working with me to get this clear.

issue_context.title: Link more aggressively to `.chain`
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

`.before` and `.after` are more cumbersome to use and more error prone than `.chain`. [Especially for scheduling](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/trait.IntoSystemConfigs.html#method.before):

> Note: The given set is not implicitly added to the schedule when this system set is added. It is safe, but no dependencies will be created.

imo that paragraph is a bit arcane for people who are not in the know about how schedules and co. exactly work
So maybe outright saying "you probably meant to use .chain()" would be good.

See [this Discord question](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/691052431974465548/1268198882001817620) for an example of a user in the wild using `.before` in code that *looks* like it would do the right thing, but actually does not.
comments:
IMO using `.before` and `.after` can almost be considered an anti-pattern at this point. If you're adding systems in the same place, use `.chain`. If you're not, use a system set.

I wouldn't necessarily suggest deprecating / removing `.before` and `.after`... but the docs should make it clear that `.chain` should be preferred unless you _really_ know better.
I heavily agree with @benfrankel on this. This issue is primarily about removing a footgun, but I'm definitely also fine with a PR advocating chain everywhere in general.

How about change the Note for `.after` and `.before` to something like:

Note: If you're adding systems in the same location, it's recommended that you use `.chain`. You can also add a set of systems.  You may want to use `.after` or `.before` for advanced scheduling and perhaps exceptional cases.

Ok, I can change the Note or keep the sentence and add the new one.

> Note: The given set is not implicitly added to the schedule when this system set is added. It is safe, but no dependencies will be created.

I am beginning with Bevy and Rust. So That sentence seems like containing useful information. Would somebody mind to explain it to me or point me to examples or similar concepts, so I could figure it out.

Thanks to this ticket and the comments here, I could understand scheduling better and how to (not) use .after/.before.

@janhohenheim Thanks for taking time. I am thinking about a concise note to describe this and replace it. I am not sure with a few things here.

You say there is a magic tric:

> ```
> struct ThisRunsInUpdate;
> struct ThisRunsInStartup;
> 
> app
>   .configure_sets(Startup, ThisRunsInStartup)
>   .configure_sets(Update, ThisRunsInUpdate);
> 
> // watch closely, here comes a magic trick
> app.configure_sets(
>   Update,
>   ThisRunsInUpdate.before(ThisRunsInStartup)
> );
> ```

And later you explain since they are in different schedules, it will be ignored. The magic trick is, that even though this could seem to work - it just won't work as one may read? Or is the magic trick is something else?
@kivi yeah, the "trick" here is that this looks correct but does absolutely nothing.

I got something (thanks to all participants of this ticket), that could work without example or we could add a simple small example with SetA, SetB or sample code as suggested in earlier comment.

__
Note: If you configure two groups of systems (let's call them 'Set A') in a Schedule, another group referencing `.after` or `.before` (let's call it 'Set B') will not be added automatically.
It's safe and won't cause any problems or errors. But no dependencies are created: Adding Set A does not automatically create any connections or relationships with Set B. They remain independent of each other.
If you're adding systems in the same location, it's **recommended** that you use **`.chain`**. You can also add a set of systems. You may want to use `.after` or `.before` for advanced planning and perhaps exceptional cases.
__

Please double check:
> It is safe, but no dependencies will be created.

I changed it to
> It's safe and won't cause any problems or errors. But no dependencies are created: Adding Set A does not automatically create any connections or relationships with Set B. They remain independent of each other.

The word **_safe_** could be misleading or maybe it's just me.
